From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: NextFin evaluation — security gates & retention options

Hi Alex / Security team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great conversation. As discussed, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the security/compliance gates we need to clear for production: SOC 2 evidence intake, SIG/CAIQ mapping, DPA redline and data retention choices.

High-level asks in the MAP:
- SOC 2: provide your expected window to receive an evidence bundle (we usually need 2 weeks from intake to stage verification).
- SIG/CAIQ: we attached our filled SIG matrix; please mark any responses you need us to expand or annotate.
- DPA: Kimberly is copied to handle redlines. Please flag the clauses you cannot accept (data residency, subprocessor list, retention limits).
- Retention: 30/90/365 day options are in the MAP; state which you need for logs, transcripts, and embeddings.

Target timeline we propose in the MAP: evaluation sign-off by 2026-02-28, legal negotiation complete by 2026-03-14, pilot go-live in early April. If you have a hard freeze date, tell us and we will adapt.

Attachments: NextFin_MAP_draft.xlsx (MAP with milestones), redwood_SIG_matrix.csv (SIG/CAIQ initial mapping), SOC2-report-stub.pdf (Redwood SOC 2 summary).

Can you confirm who on your side will own evidence intake and whether you prefer a shared drive or SFTP for document exchange? Happy to set up a short call this week to walk the MAP.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Subject: Re: MAP: NextFin evaluation — security gates & retention options

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we route to our legal and infosec owners: 

1) Evidence intake: we prefer SFTP for anything sensitive, but can do a Drive link if files are encrypted per our intake checklist. Who will run the intake from Redwood?
2) SIG matrix: I see several "TBD" rows under encryption and key management — can Jonas provide a short note on KMS/HSM approach and whether customer-managed keys are supported for private deployments?
3) Retention: default for us is 90 days for query logs and 365 days for full transcripts. Is Redwood able to scope per-customer retention at the route/model level?
4) DPA: we'll send a preliminary redline but a couple of items we expect to adjust: (a) subcontractor list; (b) EU data residency carveout; (c) deletion certification timeline.

Quick answers inline: we have an internal evidence owner (security-intake@nextfin.co) — I'll loop them if we move forward.

Can we do a follow-up call Wednesday 20 Jan 14:00 ET? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and include our legal lead.

Best,
Alex
Alex Dunne | Head of InfoSec, NextFin
alex.dunne@nextfin.co

Subject: Re: MAP: NextFin evaluation — security gates & retention options

Alex / NextFin legal & security — thanks for the quick turn. I attached our working DPA redline (DPA_redline_NextFin.docx) and a short note on retention options. High-level:

- Subprocessors: we maintain a current list; per the MAP we can provide a snapshot and commit to 30-day notice for material changes. We can include an approved subprocessors appendix in the DPA.
- Data residency: Redwood supports region-specific hosting for Private and Dedicated deployments. For Hosted accounts we offer EU residency variants in specific regions; for a contract we can add a residency annex.
- Deletion certification: standard timeframe is 30 days after request for accessible backups; longer for archived cold backups (up to 90 days) — we can negotiate a certificate-of-destruction clause.
- SOC 2 evidence: Jonas will accept a staged intake; for clarity we ask NextFin to mark which controls are in-scope for your acceptance criteria (we typically map to CC6, CC7 and CC9 controls for access, encryption, and logging).

Action items I propose now:
1) NextFin to return the SIG matrix with any "No" or "Partial" answers flagged and a short rationale by 2026-01-28.
2) NextFin legal to return DPA redline by 2026-02-05 (per Marissa's schedule).
3) Evidence intake: Jonas and Alex to confirm SFTP details during Wed call and provide secure endpoint by 2026-01-25.

If those timelines work we'll preserve the target sign-off 2026-02-28 and move legal negotiation to the first two weeks of March.

Attached: DPA_redline_NextFin.docx, SOC2-report-stub.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park | Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
